rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A complete good deed grounded in faith earns tenfold, in this life or the next; this guarantee is universal, with further reward varying according to intentions.
rows.anchor: يجازيه بذلك في الدنيا أو في الآخرة , وهذا المحقق لكل أحد ويزداد البعض وضوحا بحسب النيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the tenfold wording grammatically: the ten is treated as equivalent to the good deed and attached to its pronoun.
rows.anchor: وذكر العشر , لأنه بمعنى الحسنة , وهو مضاف إلى ضميرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person punished for an evil deed receives only its like, while God forgives much; punishment is not inevitable.
rows.anchor: فلا يجزى } أي في الدارين { إلا مثلها } إذا جوزي , ويعفو عن كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matching of punishment does not wrong anyone: no reward is reduced and no punishment increased.
rows.anchor: المماثلة موجودة في الكم والكيف , فلا ينقص أحد في ثواب ولا يزاد في عقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Equal requital would exceed human capacity, as the commands for just measure and the limit of capacity indicate, but God's knowledge and power make it easy.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى أن المساواة في الجزاء مما ينقطع دونه أعناق الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing monotheism, divine judgment and power, refuting false religions, and warning of requital, God orders Muhammad to proclaim and commend the religion revealed to him.
rows.anchor: تصحيح التوحيد بالأدلة القاطعة وتحقيق أمر القضاء والقدرة وإبطال جميع أديان الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guidance of Muhammad means both showing him the way and granting him success in following it.
rows.anchor: هدانى } أي بيانا وتوفيقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord is described as the Prophet's benefactor in every good, especially in this revelation.
rows.anchor: ربي } أي المحسن إلي بكل خير لا سيما هذا الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is a broad, clear way.
rows.anchor: طريق واسع بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr read qayyiman with an open qāf and doubled, kasra-marked yāʾ.
rows.anchor: على قراءة ابن كثير ونافع وأبي عمرو بفتح القاف وتشديد الياء المكسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use a kasra-marked qāf and light, fatḥa-marked yāʾ; this is a verbal noun meaning uprightness, used adjectivally for emphasis.
rows.anchor: في قراءة الباقين بكسر القاف وفتح الياء الخفيفة مصدر بمعنى القيام وصف به للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī explains the milla as guidance disclosed by intellect's light amid the darkness of worldly customs people have adopted.
rows.anchor: والملة ما أظهره نور العقل من الهدى في ظلم ما التزمه الناس من عوائد أمر الدنيا - أفاده الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it Abraham's religion recalls the revered forefather to people who imitate their ancestors.
rows.anchor: مذكرا لهم - لتقليدهم الآباء - بأنه دين أبيهم الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanīf means pliant and readily upright, following evidence rather than stubbornly clinging to imitation while blind to proof.
rows.anchor: لينا هينا سهلا قابلا للاستقامة لكونه ميالا مع الدليل غير جاف ولا كز واقف مع التقليد عمى عن نور الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was not among people rigidly attached to delusions, claiming a partner for God despite seeing that the alleged partner could neither harm nor benefit.
rows.anchor: الجامدين مع أوهامهم في ادعاء شريك لله مع رؤيتهم له في كونه لا يضر ولا ينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This religion is praised as the very religion God chose for Abraham, His intimate friend.
rows.anchor: وبيانا لأنه الذي اختاره سبحانه لخليله إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's question to Iblīs exposes the disbelief he had concealed, so people can learn why he was expelled.
rows.anchor: استخراجا لكفره الذي كان يخفيه بما يبدي من جوابه ليعلم الخلق سبب طرده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added negation in “why did you not prostrate?” intensifies the rebuke for refusing the commanded act.
rows.anchor: لتنفيد التأكد بالدلالة على اللوم على الامتناع من الفعل والإقدام على الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs claims superiority over Adam and says prostrating to one beneath him would be unfitting and contrary to wisdom.
rows.anchor: فلا يليق لي السجود لمن هو دوني ولا أمري بذلك لأنه مناف للحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs's argument mistakes material origins for merit: fire destroys while clay nurtures, and existence is better than nonexistence.
rows.anchor: الإيجاد خير من الإعدام بلا نزاع , والنار سبب الإعدام والمحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basis of excellence is one's end, not the elements from which one began.
rows.anchor: بل هو باعتبار الغايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because mere arrogance toward God is disbelief in any form, God answers Iblīs's refusal with expulsion rather than debate.
rows.anchor: وكان مجرد التكبر على الله كفرا على أي وجه كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Descend from it” refers to the abode Iblīs occupied, Paradise, which does not accept a sinner.
rows.anchor: مضمرا للدار التي كان فيها وهي الجنة فإنها لا تقبل عاصيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb of descent also signifies falling in rank and humiliation, fitting the surah's warning purpose.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالهبوط الذي يلزم من سقوط المنزلة دون الخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on arrogance is universal: “for you” and “in it” do not limit the prohibition to Iblīs or Paradise.
rows.anchor: ولا مفهوم لقوله ( لك ) ولا لقوله { فيها } بوجود الصرائح بالمنع من الكب مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bīqāʿī supports the universal ban on arrogance with Qur'anic warnings that God does not love the arrogant and seals the heart of every arrogant person; he also cites the passage he identifies as 4:48.
rows.anchor: وإنما قيد بذلك تهويلا للأمر فكأنه قيل لا ينبغي التكبر إلا لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Citing Muslim and other transmitters, he reports a Prophetic warning that even a mustard seed of arrogance in one's heart bars entry to Paradise.
rows.anchor: مثقال حبة من خردل كبر ) رواه مسلم وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Leave” means leaving Paradise itself, not merely moving from a higher to a lower place within it.
rows.anchor: فانتقى أن يكون الهبوط من موضع عال من الجنة إلى موضع منها أحط منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “lowly” are those fit for expulsion, distance, contempt, and disgrace.
rows.anchor: اي الذين هم أهل للطرد والبعد والحقارة والهوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having recognized that envy drove him from divine approval and lowered him, Iblīs asks for respite so he can act over an extended period.
rows.anchor: أي اجعلني موجودا بحيث أنظر واتصرف في زمن ممتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants Iblīs respite among those deferred, but not on the terms he requested; he is not preserved until the resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال إنك من المنظرين } أي في الجملة , ومنعه من الحماية عن الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “appointed time” elsewhere is the first trumpet blast, when living creatures die, including Iblīs; this surah omits the detail to make its warning more unsettling.
rows.anchor: وهو وقت النفخة الأولى التي يموت فيها الأحياء فيمون هو معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants the respite despite Iblīs's corrupt intent because he remains within God's command and decree, and the grant displays divine wisdom in reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: وأجابه إلى الأنظار وهو يريد به الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though already decreed wretched, Iblīs answers the reprieve by persisting in disbelief.
rows.anchor: وإطالة العمر بالتمادي في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bīqāʿī explains Iblīs's “You led me astray” as God's creation of error and false belief in his heart on account of humankind.
rows.anchor: وهو إيجاد الغي واعتقاد الباطل في قلبي من أجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who assign misguidance to someone other than God to absolve Him fall into a worse error by positing independent agents with conflicting wills.
rows.anchor: وقع في شر مما فر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs will persistently lie in wait throughout his reprieve, blocking obedience and drawing people into disobedience, like a highway robber ambushing travelers.
rows.anchor: في مدة إمهالك لي بقطعهم عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your straight path” is all of God's path, by the omitted preposition, and means Islam in all its branches.
rows.anchor: بما دل عليه نزع الخافض { المستقيم } وهو الإسلام بجميع شعبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording says the eyes were turned because the frightening turn itself matters, not who caused it; God turns them without their choice.
rows.anchor: بناه للمفعول لأن المخيف لهم الصرف لا كونه من معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Heights, still outside Hell and afraid of it, pray not to be placed with the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: اي أصحاب الأعراف حال كونهم لم يدخلوها وهم يخافون مستعيذين منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Heights recognize the men by their visible features; the fire has altered their appearance through burning, darkened faces, and enlarged bodies.
rows.anchor: لأن النار قد أكلتهم وغيرت معلمهم مع تغيرهم بالسمن وسواد الوجوه وعظم الجثث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They taunt the people of Hell that their wealth, supporters, and arrogance did not benefit them.
rows.anchor: أي للمال والرجال { وما كنتم تستكبرون } اي تجدون بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They point to people the arrogant had belittled and sworn would never receive God's mercy; revealing them to the damned intensifies their torment.
rows.anchor: وكأنه يكشف لهم عنهم حتى يروهم زيادة في عذابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to enter Paradise may be spoken by God or by a caller acting on His behalf; the assurance removes fear and grief.
rows.anchor: أي قال الله لهم أو قائل من قبله ادخلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once settled in Hell, its inhabitants call the people of Paradise; the Garden is made visible to them, increasing their torment.
rows.anchor: بعد أن عرفهم إياهم وامر الجنة فتزحزحت فكان ذلكزيادة في عذابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned ask those above them to pour down water or any provision because of their extreme distress.
rows.anchor: اي لأنكم اعلى منا , فإذا أفضتموه وصل إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request cannot be fulfilled: empty spaces without foothold between the Garden and the Fire prevent anything from passing between them.
rows.anchor: فإن بين النار والجنة أهوية لا قرار لها ولا يمكن وصول شيء من الدارين إلى الخر معها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has barred water and provision from the disbelievers; “disbelievers” are those who cover what sound reason and clear revelation show.
rows.anchor: الساترين لما دلهم عليه قويم العقل وصريح النقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They distorted the form and substance of their religion into diversion: heedless amusement that distracts from useful things without considering the outcome.
rows.anchor: بما من شأنه أن يغفل وينسى عن كل ما ينفع من الأمور المعجبة للنفس من غير نظر في عاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heedlessness draws people from seriousness into pleasure-seeking; “play” describes pursuing what brings pleasure and wastes the present in delusion.
rows.anchor: أي إقبالا على ما يجلب السرور ويقطع الوقت الحاضربالغرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life deceived them with transient enjoyment and veiled them from reflecting on its meaning and God's call to turn away from it.
rows.anchor: حتى صاروا بذلك محجوبين عن نظر معانيها وعما دعا إليه تعالى من الإعراض عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God leaves them like forgotten people, just as they neglected to prepare for the meeting of this Day; the abandonment of mercy is lasting.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تركهم من رحمته سبحانه مؤبداأسقط الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied God's signs despite knowing their truth, since the signs are exceptionally evident.
rows.anchor: وهم يعرفون حقيقتها لأنها في غاية الظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night covering the day is a sign of God's oneness and call to truth, sustaining bodily life; supplication should combine fear of justice with hope in grace.
rows.anchor: الدال على الوحدانية الداعي إلى الحق إقامة للأبدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining fear and hope is the station of excellence, as if seeing the Merciful: awe draws one toward mercy, and those who attain excellence deserve it.
rows.anchor: جمع بين الخوف والرجاء كان في مقام الإحسان وكأنه مشاهد للرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although raḥma is feminine, the predicate qārīb is masculine because the genitive phrase is attached to a nonfeminine noun; Bīqāʿī attributes this grammatical point to Sībawayh.
rows.anchor: لإضافتها إلى غير مؤنث فيما قال سيبوية فقال : { قريب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From the doers of excellence” replaces an explicit “from you,” generalizing the promise and tying the judgment to the quality of excellence.
rows.anchor: ولكنه اظهر تعميما وتعليقا للحكم بالوصف فقال : { من المحسنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain is one of the greatest forms of mercy, and ongoing cultivation depends on it, on clouds, and on wind; God alone sends the winds.
rows.anchor: وهو من أجل أنواع الرحمة , وهو لا يكون إلا بالسحاب , وهو لا يكون إلا بالريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use the plural “winds,” which Bīqāʿī divides into five types; Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the singular as a generic.
rows.anchor: ووحد ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي على إرادة الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the Hijazi and Basran reading, he explains the winds as spread abroad, from nashr, the dispersal of what was folded.
rows.anchor: أي منتشرة جمع نشور من النشر , وهو بسط ما كان مطويا وتفرقه في كل وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wind is not the independent cause of its own spreading, which would make it constant, nor do celestial spheres or stars cause it; their relation to the air is uniform.
rows.anchor: لا لذات الريح وإلا الدام ذلك منها ولا بقوة فلك أو نجم لأن نسبتها إلى الهواء واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before His mercy” means before rain; the two hands suggest that wind may bring mercy or punishment, though mercy is more common.
rows.anchor: أي المطر , ولعله عبر فيه باليدين : اليمنى واليسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Winds may gather or disperse clouds, pollinate and cultivate plants, or destroy them, as in autumn; they may heal or kill through heat and cold.
rows.anchor: وتارة تكون مقومة للزروع والأشجار مكملة لها وهي اللواقح , وتارة تكون منمية لها أو مهلكة كما يكون في الخريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds lift clouds because they are light in relation to them, while the clouds are heavy with water.
rows.anchor: حملتها لقلتها عندها لخفتها عليها { ثقالا } أي بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural emphasizes greatness in the winds' sending, while the singular object depicts the cloud's conveyance as one mass whose parts stay together.
rows.anchor: أفرد اللفظ دلالة على غاية العظمة بسوقه مجتمعا كأنه قطعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud is driven toward and for the sake of a dead land, one without vegetation.
rows.anchor: أي لأجله وإليه { ميت } أي بعد النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “by it” refers either to the land or to the cloud; by water, God brings forth every kind of fruit, including crops in a figurative sense.
rows.anchor: به } أي البلد , أو بسبب ذلك السحاب { الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God revives barren earth with water and restores a tree's fruit, He can raise bodies from dust and return souls; there is no difference between the two acts of bringing forth.
rows.anchor: فهو قادر على إعادة الأشباح وإيداعها الأرواح كما كانت أول مرة , لأنه لا فرق بين الإخرجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a second proof of resurrection after establishing the beginning, given so people may remember God's power to raise the dead.
rows.anchor: دليلا ثانيا في غاية الدلالة على القدرة على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bīqāʿī recalls the promise that Moses and his followers would be victorious, then frames the chiefs' response to the signs as evidence that most people are rebellious.
rows.anchor: أن أكثر الخلق فاسق , أخبر تعالى بما قال قوم فرعون بعدما رأوا من المعجز القاهر دليلا على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs are Pharaoh's notables; after the magicians believed, Pharaoh neither killed nor imprisoned Moses because he lacked the power, though he would not admit this to his people.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان لا يقدرعلى ذلك ولا يعترف به لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call Moses's reform corruption to provoke and anger Pharaoh, presenting the change of religion as his intended mischief.
rows.anchor: سموه فسادا وجعلوه مقصودا لفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed view says Pharaoh had ordered his people to worship idols as a means of drawing near to him.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان أمر قومه أن يعبدوا الأصنام تقريبا إليه

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī considers Pharaoh more likely a materialist who denied a Creator and held that planets govern the lower world; he may have made and worshipped idols in their images.
rows.anchor: الأقرب أنه كان دهريا منكرا لوجود الصانع , وكان يقول : مدبر هذا العالم للخلق السفلي هو الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bīqāʿī connects that account of Pharaoh's beliefs with his claim to be the highest lord.
rows.anchor: أنه كان قد اتخذ أصناما على صور الكواكب ويعبدها على ما هو دين عبده الكواكب انتهى . ولذلك قال :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An interpretation of Pharaoh's “gods” is reported, but Bīqāʿī says it does not fit the comparison; he instead reads the term as a title for Pharaoh and the rulers under him.
rows.anchor: هكذا قيل , وهوظاهر عبارة التوارة الآتية في آية القمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bīqāʿī's preferred sense is that Pharaoh was called a god and assigned each prince a people who treated him as one, since Egyptians called rulers and chiefs gods.
rows.anchor: بل الظاهر أنه كان سمى امراءة آلهة , وسمى لكل أمير قوما يتألهونه أي يطيعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this political usage, Pharaoh's chiefs are subordinate gods or rulers, while Moses and the Israelites are subjects with no ruler among them, so the chiefs ask why Pharaoh would leave them alone.
rows.anchor: فحيث وقعت الموازنة بين موسى عليه السلام وقومه وبين فرعون وقومه , عبر بالآلهه تعظيما لجانبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh denies any other god when addressing his chiefs but tells the gathered people he is the highest lord; Bīqāʿī links these audience-specific claims to 28:38 and 79:24.
rows.anchor: وحيث نفي افلهية عن غيره فبالنظر إلى خطابه للملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turned a ruler's figurative title into literal divinity and granted rulers divine authority to declare things lawful or forbidden, like taking rabbis and monks as lords.
rows.anchor: فجعلوه حقيقة وصاروا يفعلون ما يختص به الالهة من التحليل والتحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their accusation was that Pharaoh accepted parity by letting himself rule the Copts and Moses rule the Israelites as separate, equal leaders.
rows.anchor: رئيسا على القبط وموسى عليه السلام رئيسا على بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though God had checked Pharaoh's earlier killing of Israelite sons while drawing him toward destruction, Pharaoh now threatens renewed slaughter and sparing the women, claiming he remains dominant.
rows.anchor: أي تقتيلا كثيرا { أبناءهم } أي كما كنا نفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh portrays his inaction toward Moses as indifference, hoping people will not believe the prophecy that an Israelite child would end his rule and turn against him.
rows.anchor: موهما بهذا أن تركه لأذى موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses tells the Israelites to seek help from God through worship that pleases Him and to remain patient.
rows.anchor: أي الصقوا طلب العون { بالله } الذي لا أعظم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All land, Egypt and beyond, belongs to God alone; the repetition emphasizes His greatness, exclusive authority, and blessing.
rows.anchor: كرره تذكيرا بالعظمة وتصريحا وتبركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants the earth as an inheritance to whichever servants He wills; all are equal in relation to Him.
rows.anchor: ولما أخبر أن نسبة الكل إليه واحدة , أخبر بما يرفع بعضهم على فقال : { والعاقبة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final outcome belongs to the God-fearing, who protect themselves from God's anger by doing what pleases Him; present hardship may be a trial or a prelude to ruin.
rows.anchor: أي الذين يقون أنفسهم سخط الله بعمل ما يرضيه فلا عبرة بما ترون في العاجل فإنه قد يكون استدراجا
